title: Getting started with rectangler
text: rectangler designed comparing small number meaningful objects. objects can domains, groups, categories, steps, indicators units remain directly readable. package useful want something diagram-like bar chart, open readable treemap. treemap usually packs objects inside one larger rectangle. rectangler keeps objects separate. bar chart usually uses equal-width bars. rectangler uses rectangular layouts, labels, shapes annotations build compact comparison graphics.

title: Getting started with rectangler
text: rectangler based three simple ideas: constructors create layouts; layers add information; visual sizes mostly relative. means can start simple layout enrich step step.
code: rect_plot4(data) %>%   rect_style() %>%   rect_label() %>%   rect_shape() %>%   rect_shape_label() %>%   rect_annotation()

title: Getting started with rectangler
text: examples vignette use four fictional domains.
code: mydata <- tibble::tibble(   value = c(2643, 6939, 2227, 3764),   label = c("D1", "D2", "D3", "D4"),   border = c("#3B82A0", "#6A994E", "#D17A22", "#A44A6F"),   fill = c("#E7F2F7", "#EDF5E7", "#FBF0E3", "#F6E8EF"),   shape_fill = c("#3B82A0", "#6A994E", "#D17A22", "#A44A6F"),   annotation = c(     "Top performer",     "Highest growth",     "Largest investment",     "Lowest cost"   ) ) %>%   mutate(     share = round(value / sum(value) * 100),     text = paste0(value, "\n(", share, "%)")   )

title: Getting started with rectangler
text: Every rectangler graphic starts constructor. constructor creates basic rectangular layout.  Layers add styling, labels, shapes annotations.     grammar used throughout package:
code: rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label_col = "text",     size = 0.8   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label_col = "text",     size = 0.8   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     fill = "white",     border_colour = mydata$border,     border_width = 1.5   ) %>%   rect_shape_label(     label_col = "label",     size = 1.2   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label_col = "text",     size = 0.8   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     fill = "white",     border_colour = mydata$border,     border_width = 1.5   ) %>%   rect_shape_label(     label_col = "label",     size = 1.2   ) %>%   rect_annotation(     label_col = "annotation",     position = "horizontal",     space = 1   ) constructor(data) %>%   layer() %>%   layer() %>%   layer()

title: Getting started with rectangler
text: rect_style() controls fill, border colour, border width, border type transparency rectangles.  fixed value applied rectangles.  vector gives one value per rectangle.  column argument reads values data.
code: rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour = "#3B82A0",     border_width = 2   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour = c("#3B82A0", "#6A994E", "#D17A22", "#A44A6F"),     border_width = c(1, 2, 3, 4)   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill_col = "fill",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   )

title: Getting started with rectangler
text: rect_label() adds text inside rectangles.  Labels can also supplied directly.
code: rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(label_col = "text") rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),     size = 1.2   )

title: Getting started with rectangler
text: rect_shape() adds small shapes rectangles. Shapes can used markers, category badges visual anchors.  rect_shape_label() adds text shapes.  Shape positions can adjusted.  Offsets move shapes without changing rectangles.
code: rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     fill_col = "shape_fill",     border_colour = "white",     border_width = 1   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     fill_col = "shape_fill",     border_colour = "white",     border_width = 1   ) %>%   rect_shape_label(     label_col = "label",     colour = "white",     size = 1.1   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     fill_col = "shape_fill",     border_colour = "white",     border_width = 1   ) %>%   rect_shape_label(     label_col = "label",     colour = "white",     size = 1.1   )  rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "top-bottom",     fill_col = "shape_fill",     border_colour = "white",     border_width = 1   ) %>%   rect_shape_label(     position = "top-bottom",     label_col = "label",     colour = "white",     size = 1.1   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     offset_x = 0,     offset_y = 0,     fill_col = "shape_fill",     border_colour = "white"   )  rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     offset_x = 0.4,     offset_y = 0.4,     fill_col = "shape_fill",     border_colour = "white"   )

title: Getting started with rectangler
text: rect_annotation() adds comments around layout. Annotations useful plot explain object matters.  Annotation positions can use intuitive names. example, position = "horizontal" position = "h" mean horizontal annotations.
code: rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_colour_col = "border",     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label_col = "label",     size = 1   ) %>%   rect_annotation(     label_col = "annotation",     position = "horizontal",     space = 1   ) rect_annotation(position = "horizontal") rect_annotation(position = "h")

text: Rectangler designed comparison graphics small number objects remain visually distinct directly readable. Unlike treemaps, keeps objects separate instead packing single area. Unlike bar charts, combines rectangular layouts labels, shapes annotations create compact comparison graphics. Design principles constructor + layer grammar four built-layouts publication-ready comparison graphics works naturally ggplot2

title: Create Rectangle-Based Comparison Plots
text: Let’s build simple Rectangler graphic step step. Create example data. Start constructor.  Add styling.  Add labels.  Add corner shapes.  Add labels shapes.  Add annotations final layer.
code: mydata <- tibble::tibble(   value = c(2643, 6939, 2227, 3764),   label = c("D1", "D2", "D3", "D4"),   border = c("#3B82A0", "#6A994E", "#D17A22", "#A44A6F"),   annotation = c(     "Top performer",     "Highest growth",     "Largest investment",     "Lowest cost"   ) ) %>%   mutate(     share = round(value / sum(value) * 100),     text = paste0(value, "\n(", share, "%)")   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_color = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_color = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label_col = "text",     size = 0.8   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_color = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label_col = "text",     size = 0.8   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     fill = "white",     border_color = mydata$border,     border_width = 1.5   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_color = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label_col = "text",     size = 0.8   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     fill = "white",     border_color = mydata$border,     border_width = 1.5   ) %>%   rect_shape_label(     label_col = "label",     size = 1.2   ) rect_plot4(mydata, value_col = "value") %>%   rect_style(     fill = "white",     border_color = mydata$border,     border_width = 2   ) %>%   rect_label(     label_col = "text",     size = 0.8   ) %>%   rect_shape(     position = "corner",     fill = "white",     border_color = mydata$border,     border_width = 1.5   ) %>%   rect_shape_label(     label_col = "label",     size = 1.2   ) %>%   rect_annotation(     label_col = "annotation",     position = "horizontal",     size = 0.6,     space = 1   )

text: Creates horizontal layout rectangles arranged left right. Rectangle areas proportional values value_col. returned plot can customised adding Rectangler layers, rect_style(), rect_label(), rect_shape(), rect_shape_label(), rect_annotation().

title: Create a row layout of rectangles — rect_row
code: rect_row(   data = rect_data_demo,   value_col = "value",   aspect_ratio = "square",   gap = rect_defaults$gap,   padding = rect_defaults$padding,   align = "bottom" )

title: Create a row layout of rectangles — rect_row
text: data data frame containing one row rectangle. value_col Name column containing rectangle values. aspect_ratio Desired rectangle aspect ratio. Can "square", "golden", ratio string "1:2", numeric vector c(1, 2). gap Relative spacing rectangles. padding Relative padding around complete layout. align Alignment rectangles within row. One "top" "bottom".

title: Create a row layout of rectangles — rect_row
text: Rectangler plot object (ggplot) can extended additional Rectangler layer functions.

title: Create a row layout of rectangles — rect_row
code: rect_row()   rect_row(rect_data_demo, align = "bottom")

what: Add shapes to a Rectangler plot — rect_shape
title: Add shapes to a Rectangler plot — rect_shape
text: Adds one shape rectangle Rectangler plot. Shapes can placed inside near rectangles, appearance can set directly mapped columns original data.

title: Add shapes to a Rectangler plot — rect_shape
code: rect_shape(   plot,   position = NULL,   offset_x = 0,   offset_y = 0,   shape = NULL,   shape_col = NULL,   size = NULL,   size_col = NULL,   fill = NULL,   fill_col = NULL,   border_colour = NULL,   border_color = NULL,   border_colour_col = NULL,   border_color_col = NULL,   border_width = NULL,   border_width_col = NULL )

title: Add shapes to a Rectangler plot — rect_shape
text: plot Rectangler plot created rect_plot4(), rect_row(), rect_col(), rect_pyr(). position Shape position. NULL, default "corner" rect_plot4() "top-right" layouts. offset_x Horizontal offset relative rectangle width. offset_y Vertical offset relative rectangle height. shape Shape value passed ggplot2::geom_point(). shape_col Name column containing shape values. size Shape size. size_col Name column containing shape sizes. fill Shape fill colour. fill_col Name column containing shape fill colours. border_colour Shape border colour. border_color Alias border_colour. border_colour_col Name column containing shape border colours. border_color_col Alias border_colour_col. border_width Shape border width. border_width_col Name column containing shape border widths.

title: Add shapes to a Rectangler plot — rect_shape
text: Rectangler plot object added shape layer.

title: Add shapes to a Rectangler plot — rect_shape
code: rect_plot4() %>%   rect_shape()   rect_plot4(rect_data_demo) %>%   rect_shape(position = "top-right", shape = 21, fill = "white")

title: Add labels to shapes — rect_shape_label
